data_section_full_text:
2.1. Sample Selection Criteria

First Call maintains a database of prospective earnings-related announcements made by
companies after September 1992. From the First Call database, we obtained the cusip,
company name, date, and a summary of the disclosed information pertaining to quarterly
earnings for the 929 announcements for which both the preannouncement date and the earnings announcement date were before December 1995. We eliminated 19 announcements
for which the cusip was incorrect or missing. Since it is difficult to compare disclosures that
are qualitative in nature to actual earnings amounts, we also eliminated 32 announcements
which did not contain a quantitative reference to upcoming quarterly earnings. We required
that the earnings announcement date and actual earnings per share amounts were available
in the Compustat database; 816 observations met this data requirement. We eliminated 195
announcements for which returns were not available in the CRSP database, or for which no
analyst forecasts for the announcement quarter appeared in the Zacks Investment Research
database (Zacks) in the 120 days prior to the announcement. To minimize potential errors,
we also eliminated 23 observations for which the formal earnings announcement date occurred more than 60 days after the end of the quarter, and three observations for which
the announcement date from First Call was after the formal earnings announcement date
reported by Compustat. We also eliminated 12 announcements issued before the beginning
of the quarter to which they pertained.

To ensure the validity of the data and comparability between data from Zacks and Compustat, we checked actual earnings amounts against press releases for all firms for which
there was at least a ten-cent difference between actual earnings per share as reported by
Compustat and the comparable consensus analyst forecast we computed from the Zacks
data. We also checked both the actual earnings amount and the tentative earnings amount
for all announcements for which there was at least a three-cent per share difference be

tween actual and preannounced earnings. We corrected erroneous data and eliminated 42
observations for which we could not verify the amounts on LEXIS / NEXIS. <sup>4</sup>

We coded the remaining 541 announcements according to their “types.” We used four
preannouncement types: a point estimate, a range, a statement that earnings will be greater
than some amount, and a statement that earnings will be less than some amount. Because of
the difficulty in quantifying the expectations implied by “greater than” and “less than” preannouncements, we limited our analysis to the 429 point and range preannouncements. As a
result, our results may not generalize to other preannouncement types. We further required
that these point and range preannouncements be made no more than two weeks before the
end of the quarter. <sup>5</sup> We imposed this requirement to minimize the possibility that intervening events affected the manager’s information significantly between the preannouncement
and the earnings announcement. Thus, for our sample observations, it is easier to consider
the difference between actual earnings and preannounced earnings as intentional. The final
sample contains 335 preannouncement observations from 1993
